Seminar Title:

Dynamic characterization of Graphene origami enabled metamaterial auxetic composite structures

Jonnalagadda Srinivas

Abstract:

Graphene origami (GOri)-enabled auxetic metamaterials have attracted considerable attention because their mechanical properties can be tailored through graphene content, folding degree, and thickness-wise distribution. In the present study, the vibration behaviour of a functionally graded GOri-reinforced copper beam is investigated using the first-order shear deformation theory (FSDT) within the Timoshenko beam framework. The beam is modelled using three degrees of freedom, namely axial displacement, transverse displacement, and cross-sectional rotation. The effective properties of the GOri/Cu layers are evaluated using a Halpin&ndashTsai-based micromechanical model with the corresponding correction functions for graphene content and folding degree.. The governing formulation is developed using Hamilton&rsquos principle, while a continuous reduced-order weighted-residual approach is employed to obtain the natural frequencies. Parametric investigations are then performed to examine the effects of graphene weight fraction, folding degree, beam slenderness ratio, and number of layers on the natural frequencies. Further multi-objective optimization, sandwich beam design for blast loads, debonding studies of such sandwich beam is to analyze under cyclic load, and experimental work is to be done in future.
